From ddd9b5e3e765d8ed5a35786a6cb00111713fe161 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jouni Hogander <jouni.hogander@unikie.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Dec 2019 13:46:34 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] net-sysfs: Call dev_hold always in rx_queue_add_kobject

Dev_hold has to be called always in rx_queue_add_kobject.
Otherwise usage count drops below 0 in case of failure in
kobject_init_and_add.

Fixes: b8eb718348b8 ("net-sysfs: Fix reference count leak in rx|netdev_queue_add_kobject")
Reported-by: syzbot <syzbot+30209ea299c09d8785c9@syzkaller.appspotmail.com>
Cc: Tetsuo Handa <penguin-kernel@I-love.SAKURA.ne.jp>
Cc: David Miller <davem@davemloft.net>
Cc: Lukas Bulwahn <lukas.bulwahn@gmail.com>
Signed-off-by: Jouni Hogander <jouni.hogander@unikie.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/net/core/net-sysfs.c b/net/core/net-sysfs.c
index 5c4624298996..4c826b8bf9b1 100644
--- a/net/core/net-sysfs.c
+++ b/net/core/net-sysfs.c
@@ -919,14 +919,17 @@ static int rx_queue_add_kobject(struct net_device *dev, int index)
 	struct kobject *kobj = &queue->kobj;
 	int error = 0;
 
+	/* Kobject_put later will trigger rx_queue_release call which
+	 * decreases dev refcount: Take that reference here
+	 */
+	dev_hold(queue->dev);
+
 	kobj->kset = dev->queues_kset;
 	error = kobject_init_and_add(kobj, &rx_queue_ktype, NULL,
 				     "rx-%u", index);
 	if (error)
 		goto err;
 
-	dev_hold(queue->dev);
-
 	if (dev->sysfs_rx_queue_group) {
 		error = sysfs_create_group(kobj, dev->sysfs_rx_queue_group);
 		if (error)
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `net/core/net-sysfs.c`**
- The line `dev_hold(queue->dev);` was moved to the beginning of the `rx_queue_add_kobject` function. This ensures that the device reference count is incremented before any potential failure in the subsequent operations.
- The original line `dev_hold(queue->dev);` that was located after the `kobject_init_and_add` call was removed. This change prevents the reference count from being decremented below zero if `kobject_init_and_add` fails.

### Relationships Between Modifications
The modification ensures that the device reference count is always incremented when entering the `rx_queue_add_kobject` function, regardless of whether the kobject initialization succeeds or fails. This change addresses a bug where the reference count could drop below zero if an error occurred during the kobject initialization, thus preventing potential use-after-free issues. The relationship between the modifications is that the new placement of `dev_hold` guarantees proper reference counting, enhancing the stability and reliability of the code.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
error = kobject_init_and_add(kobj, &rx_queue_ktype, NULL, "rx-%u", index);
```
```c
kobject_put(kobj);
```
Reason:
The `kobject_init_and_add` function can fail, and if it does, the reference count of the device is not incremented by `dev_hold`, leading to a potential situation where the reference count drops below zero. This can cause a use-after-free error when the device is accessed after it has been released, especially since `kobject_put` is called later, which decreases the reference count.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
dev_hold(queue->dev);
```
Reason:
By calling `dev_hold(queue->dev);` before `kobject_init_and_add`, the reference count of the device is incremented regardless of whether `kobject_init_and_add` succeeds or fails. This ensures that the reference count does not drop below zero, preventing the use-after-free error when the device is accessed later.
